copy.blurb:
New Zealand face Belgium on Saturday, overnight UTC kickoff, in FIFA World Cup 2026. This is one of the matches where the model's number disagrees with the closing line on Polymarket — a substantive gap on the New Zealand side, +6.7pp.

On Elo, Belgium comes in 310 points ahead — New Zealand at 1550, Belgium at 1860. Both Elo numbers are pulled live from the public Elo source. The adjustment layer is quiet on this fixture — no host bonus, no home-ground correction, no altitude folding in. The Elo numbers above are what the model uses.

Three-way split from the model: New Zealand to win at 13%, the draw at 11%, and Belgium to win at 76%. Draw share decays with Elo gap; on a fixture this evenly matched the draw carries more probability than a casual reader might guess. New Zealand on the win side reads 13%.

On the same three-way, Polymarket: New Zealand to win at 6%, the draw at 13%, and Belgium to win at 80%. Polymarket has New Zealand at 6%, which prices out at American odds of +1567; the model has the same side at 13%. The +6.7pp gap across them is the disagreement we're surfacing.

Pick gate is a lower-bound check, not the point estimate. A 100-sample bootstrap perturbs the Elo prior (±20), the host bonus (±15), and the altitude bonus (±10), then reads the 5th-percentile probability back out. On the New Zealand side that lower bound is 9% — +3.5pp clear of the market's 6%, comfortably past our +3pp threshold. The claim is narrow: on this fixture, on this side, the price is below what the underlying read supports. We don't argue the market is broadly wrong — across the priced field the model and the line agree more often than they disagree. We surface the ones where they don't.

The read above is the most recent one, not a frozen call. With kickoff 32 days out, the refresh is weekly until we cross five days, then daily, then hourly inside the final day. Injury news, the actual XI, and conditions at kickoff all change what the model sees. We re-publish on every refresh. The page shows what the engine reads; what to do with that information is a reader's call.
drivers: Bootstrap lower-bound on the New Zealand side still clears the Pick threshold.
Editorial analysis only — Odds Primer does not place trades or recommend a wager.
Pre-match Elo gives New Zealand a stronger prior than the Polymarket line implies.
The +6.7pp gap clears the Desk's 3 percentage point threshold for a Pick.
copy.summary: The home side reads stronger to the model than to the market. Our Elo prior puts New Zealand at 13%; Polymarket prices that side at 6%. The +6.7pp gap calls a Pick.
copy.title: New Zealand v Belgium · the model leans New Zealand
